1 3.

As per prosecution story, a complaint was lodged by the complainant Dharmendra alleging therein that Bhaskar Credit Cooperative Society, Head Office Bharroli Road, Near IPS School, Bhind through its agents/employees working at its Branch Office- Branch Bundela Colony, Jai Hospital Ke Makan, Purani Collectorate Ke Pichhe, Datia lured the complainant and other customers to invest money in the aforesaid Cooperative Society with the promise to return the same with interest and thereby took total amount of Rs.47,00,000/- from the complainant and other customers, but did not return the said amount after the maturity period.

Cheques for an amount of Rs.27,00,000/-
were provided to the complainant by the accused persons, but the same were also dishonoured due to insufficient fund in the bank account.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant's cooperative society, namely, Bhaskar Credit Cooperative Society has already returned the amount of most of the policy holders.
Out of 25 policy holders, 17 persons have received their amount.
Due to financial constraints, the amount payable to the complainant could not be paid, but applicant's Cooperative Society is ready to return the amount payable to him.
Applicant has not committed any offence.
He has falsely been implicated in the matter only because of the fact that he is Manager of the aforesaid Cooperative Society.
His custodial interrogation is not required, as the prosecution case is based on documentary evidence.
Therefore, the applicant be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted affidavits of 17 policy holders in support of his above submissions, wherein they have admitted that they have received their policy amount.
This Court vide order dated 6.9.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.39887/2023 has granted bail to co-accused Uday Singh Kushwah.

4.1 Learned counsel for the applicant in the alternative has submitted that as the offences alleged against the applicant are punishable not more than seven years of imprisonment, therefore,
applicant's application may be disposed of in the light of directions given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar & another [(2014) 8 SCC 273].
5.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the application and submits that applicant alongwith other co-accused persons being the Branch Manager of Bhaskar Credit Cooperative Society, Branch Bundela Colony, Jai Hospital Ke Makan, Purani Collectorate Ke Pichhe,
Datia misappropriated the huge amount.

sentences.text: Offences alleged against the applicant are serious in nature, therefore, he is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.

6. Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.
7.

Having considered rival submissions and nature of allegations alleged against the applicant,
although the applicant does not deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail, but considering the fact that all the offences alleged against the applicant are punishable with not more than 7 years of imprisonment and Section 41(1) of Cr.P.C. provides that the offences for which punishment prescribed is imprisonment for a term upto seven years, the accused may be kept in custody only if the condition enumerated under Section 41(1)(b)(ii) of Cr.P.C. exists as well as considering the fact that in the case of Arnesh Kumar (supra), the Apex Court has held as under:-
"..........the arrest effected by the police officer does not satisfy the requirements of Section 41 of the Code, Magistrate is duty bound not to authorize his further Mahendra Singh Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185114248/
2 detention and release the accused......".

entities.text: Mahendra Singh Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
therefore, in view of the observations laid down in the judgement referred above, I deem it fit to direct as under :-
(i) That, the police may resort to the extreme step of arrest only when the same is necessary and the applicant fails to cooperate in the investigation.
(ii) That, the applicant should first be summoned to cooperate in the investigation.
If the applicant cooperates in the investigation, then the occasion of his arrest should not arise.

(iii) That, if the applicant-accused person is arrested and he wants to file application under Section 437 of Cr.P.C. for regular bail before lower Court, then he will be produced before the lower Court without any delay.

7.1 Lower Court is also directed to consider his bail application as expeditiously as possible,
preferably, on the same day.
7.2 This application is disposed of with the aforesaid directions.
7.3 Certified copy, as per Rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE (alok) ALOK KUMAR 2023.09.19 17:33:35 +05'30'
